content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Ground-penetrating radar surveys with multiple frequency antennas can detect previously undocumented utility segments and identify conflict points when overlaid with design drawings, supporting conflict detection and route revision in areas with documentation gaps.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-06293","field":"abstract","quote":"GPR surveys with 250 MHz and 500 MHz antennas were conducted prior to open-cut construction; results were overlaid with cable route design drawings to identify conflict points. Seventeen previously unknown utility segments were discovered"}]},{"text":"Integration of multiple positioning techniques including RTK-GNSS with total-station traverses can achieve sub-5-centimetre horizontal accuracy for utility location in constrained urban environments where satellite signals are obstructed.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-01829","field":"abstract","quote":"A workflow combining short RTK observation windows with constrained total-station traverses bridging signal gaps reduced the lane-canyon horizontal RMS to 3.8 cm"}]},{"text":"Subsurface utility engineering methodologies encompassing desk study, geophysical detection, and test-hole verification can identify root causes of documentation gaps such as informal network extensions and support structured processes for cable burial programmes.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-06293","field":"abstract","quote":"The chapter discusses root causes of documentation gaps, including informal network extensions during the 1980s and post-war reconstruction, and proposes a project-phase checklist"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher's publications directly address legacy underground cable detection through GPR and integrated positioning methods [SYN-PUB-06293, SYN-PUB-01829], and her expertise in subsurface utility engineering, GIS cadastre compilation, and conflict detection matches the challenge's core requirement to locate poorly documented 1970s–1980s cables and reduce exploratory pit requirements [R0539]."}
